subject: Proposal: bundle swap + pro-rated top-up with SLA carve-out
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@solventai.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: support@solventai.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial question on mid-contract capacity and SLA adjust

Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran a quick internal review and have two asks before we take anything to procurement: 1) can the additional capacity be pro-rated to the quarter rather than annualized? We're mid-quarter and doing annualization will materially overcommit us, 2) we need an explicit carve-out in the SLA for the additional burst GPU pool — legal wants to separate the guaranteed latency SLA for our baseline reserved pool from best-effort burst instances.

I attached a short note with what Procurement needs as a minimum. If you can reply with a proposal we can review with Finance next week.

– Elena

----
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@solventai.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 17:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial question on mid-contract capacity and SLA adjust

Elena — appreciated the call. I added Ben (pricing) and Irene (legal) to loop them in. High level thoughts below; I can turn this into a one-page amendment and SOW once you confirm approach.

Proposal overview (quick):
- Bundle swap: move 25% of their unused annual seat/commit value into a quarterly "burst" bucket redeemable for accelerated inference capacity. This reduces annualized top-up exposure.
- Pro-rate rule: additional consumption applied to the burst bucket will be billed pro-rated to the end of the current billing quarter (not annualized).
- SLA carve-out: baseline reserved capacity keeps SLA:T1 latency SLA (99.9 p95). Burst bucket operates under 'best-effort' latency with a soft-SLA and a credit cap; we'll make performance guidance explicit in the SOW and a fallback rule to baseline if burst latency degrades beyond threshold.
- Pricing: nominal uplift of 18% on per-token/GPU-hour pricing for burst usage vs baseline (reflects priority and capacity overhead). We can offer a 10% one-time credit if they convert the burst to a baseline reserved add-on within the next 90 days.

Open items for Elena/Procurement to confirm: whether the burst bucket needs region restriction, and whether billing must produce separate line items for baseline vs burst.

If that all looks sensible I'll draft the amendment and SOW with explicit metrics and example math.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: SolventAI_followup_requirements.pdf (1 page, PDF)

----
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal review — pricing sanity check

Quick notes from pricing:
- 18% uplift on burst looks reasonable vs baseline; suggest we round to 20% if we want cleaner math in the SOW and to preserve margin in peak weeks.
- The 10% conversion credit is generous; recommend limiting to customers who convert >= 50% of burst capacity into baseline to avoid gaming.
- Help me with a worked example (baseline commit, current usage, proposed burst size) and I'll back into exact per-token/GPU-hour numbers and expected monthly revenue impact.

Also cc'd Prod Ops for the soft-SLA language — Irene, can we codify the performance guidance and the fallback rule to baseline in a way that is operationally verifiable (traces, p95 windows, and a runbook)?

— Ben

----
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@solventai.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: bundle swap + pro-rated top-up with SLA carve-out

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the patience while we drafted language. I've attached a short SOW draft and a one-page amendment that lays out: pro-rate billing to quarter end; separate invoice line items; soft-SLA definition for "burst" (best-effort p95 guidance, monitoring hooks, and a maximum credit of 5% of monthly invoice if soft-SLA is missed more than twice in a 30-day window); and the conversion credit mechanics (50% conversion min to claim the 10% credit).

Key callouts:
- We cannot put the burst instances under the same latency SLA as baseline without significant operational changes. The carve-out language includes an explicit fallback: if burst latency exceeds p95 threshold for three consecutive 10-minute windows, requests should be routed to baseline capacity and a short incident runbook triggers (notification + temporary billing cap).
- For procurement: we can provide a 30-day audit report for the burst bucket (usage and p95 stats) on request.

Next steps: Marissa — if you can confirm region restriction and the example numbers Ben requested, I will finalize the amendment and route to Legal for signature-ready copies.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Attachment: SOW_topup_draft.docx (3 pages)
